core_obligations: Reduce to a quasi-compact base and bound the dimension (proof lines 18899-18910): it suffices to treat quasi-compact Y and Y'; the fibre dimensions of f and f' are bounded, so the proper dimension lemma gives that f_* and f'_* have finite cohomological dimension in the sense of the unbounded derived-category lemma.
Choose a good representative (proof lines 18911-18918): take a K-injective complex I^bullet of Z/nZ-modules whose terms are injective sheaves and which represents E.

Compute both sides (proof lines 18919-18935): the usual proper base change theorem gives R^q f'_*(g')^{-1}I^n = 0 for q > 0, so the acyclicity lemma lets one compute Rf'_*(g')^{-1}E by the complex f'_*(g')^{-1}I^bullet; another application of proper base change identifies that complex with g^{-1}f_*I^bullet, which is the assertion.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a quasi-compact base and use the fibre dimension bound to get finite cohomological dimension.
Represent E by a K-injective complex with injective terms.
Use acyclicity plus the usual proper base change theorem to identify the two sides.
difficulty_reason: The lemma extends proper base change to unbounded complexes of Z/nZ-modules (statement lines 18886-18896). The proof (proof lines 18898-18935) reduces to a quasi-compact base, obtains finite cohomological dimension of the two pushforwards from the fibre dimension bound, chooses a K-injective representative with injective terms, and uses the acyclicity lemma together with the usual proper base change theorem in each degree to identify the two complexes. H2: one dimension reduction plus one acyclicity computation, written out.
